frameworks.name: C-L-O-S-E-R Sales Script Framework
frameworks.definition: A question-based call structure: Clarify why the prospect is there, Label them with their problem, Overview their past experiences and pains, Sell by invitation (get invited to pitch), Explain solutions to 2-3 of their stated problems, then address concerns and Reinforce the decision.

frameworks.name: Sales Manager Daily Feedback Loop
frameworks.definition: A structured 60-minute per-rep weekly cadence: 30 minutes reviewing 1-2 recorded calls at 2x speed with written notes, 5 minutes communicating the top 1-2 highest-impact improvements, 25 minutes role-playing those specific improvements with the rep.

frameworks.name: Sales Team Culture Triad
frameworks.definition: Three levers for maintaining sales team culture and performance: (1) a live visual leaderboard, (2) KPI-linked competitions every 4-6 weeks, (3) mandatory bottom-10% quarterly cuts.

claims.text: Alex Hormozi tests sales candidate coachability during interviews by giving a brief role-play scenario, then providing one piece of feedback and asking the candidate to try again. If the candidate accepts the feedback without ego resistance and improves on the second attempt, they are coachable; if they resist feedback, Hormozi treats this as a reliable early predictor that they will fail on the team.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Sales rep hiring process
Any sales role
claims.mechanism: Coachability under low-stakes feedback predicts coachability under high-stakes live-call feedback; ego resistance in a no-pressure interview predicts ego resistance when real money is on the line.

claims.text: Alex Hormozi argues that prospect knowledge is underemphasized relative to product knowledge in sales onboarding: understanding the prospect's problems so deeply that you can articulate them back verbatim causes the prospect to believe you intrinsically understand their situation, which drives purchase regardless of the specific product being sold.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: High-touch sales conversations
Any product or service where the prospect has a felt problem
claims.mechanism: When a salesperson mirrors a prospect's problem back to them precisely, the prospect infers that the seller understands their situation at the expert level. This inference of expert understanding transfers to trust in the solution, making the specific product secondary to the diagnostic credibility.
bounded_by: Does not apply to transactional self-serve purchases where the buyer already knows what they want

claims.text: Alex Hormozi structures new sales rep onboarding as a 14-day program: the first phase requires the trainee to listen to approximately 40 recorded sales calls (good ones), study a question-based script, and role-play every morning before being placed on a half-schedule for live calls. A full schedule is only granted after the trainee meets a minimum close-rate threshold (minimum allowable KPI).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: New sales hire
Service or B2B sales environment

claims.text: Alex Hormozi argues that a question-based scripted framework outperforms open-ended or improvised sales conversations because it leads the prospect naturally to a single binary decision (yes/no on whether the service can help them more than their current path). Salespeople who ask 'do you have any questions for me?' instead of following the script are signaling they don't know how to close, because they are inviting the prospect to generate more objections rather than directing them to a decision.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: B2B or high-touch service sales calls
Single-call close environment
claims.mechanism: An unstructured call produces an unstructured outcome. A scripted question sequence narrows the conversation to one decision axis (can we help you more than your alternative?), reducing cognitive load on the buyer and leaving no ambiguous exit ramps. Asking 'do you have any questions?' opens exit ramps.
bounded_by: Does not apply to enterprise multi-stakeholder sales with long decision cycles

claims.text: Alex Hormozi's sales manager review process allocates time as follows: 30 minutes reviewing 1-2 recorded calls at 2x speed with written notes, 5 minutes on the call communicating the 1-2 highest-impact improvements only (not all deficiencies), and 25 minutes drilling those specific improvements through role-play. Feedback is then sent in writing after the call.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Ongoing sales reps on full schedule
Weekly 1-on-1 sales manager cadence

numbers.axis: Sales manager 1-on-1 session time allocation (60 min total per rep per week)

claims.text: Alex Hormozi states that the best salesperson on a team is rarely the best sales manager. Sales managers tend to be more even-tempered, more giving, and psychologically stable, with fewer emotional highs and lows than top closers. Sales managers must be the rock the team looks up to, not the top performer who the team fears.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Sales organizations of any size
Roles: top closer vs. team manager

claims.text: Alex Hormozi argues that a sales manager's core job is to motivate and train, not to run pipeline reviews or status meetings. Sales management is fundamentally a tolerance skill: the manager who tolerates the most underperformance produces the weakest team, because tolerance of low standards communicates implicitly that low standards are acceptable.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Any sales team
Manager in an active coaching role
claims.mechanism: Teams interpret what managers tolerate as the implicit minimum standard. If a manager allows missed pipeline hygiene, late arrivals, or missed scripts without consequence, the team infers that these standards are negotiable, and underperformance spreads to the median performer.

claims.text: Alex Hormozi's sales team culture framework requires cutting the bottom 10% of performers on a quarterly basis. Without regular cuts, the team observes that underperformance has no consequence, which degrades culture across the entire team, including high performers who begin to relax standards.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Sales teams of any size
On a quarterly review cadence
claims.mechanism: Retention of low performers sends a signal to the entire team that the floor is negotiable. High performers observe underperforming peers without consequences and recalibrate their own effort floor downward. Cuts signal that the floor is real.

claims.text: Alex Hormozi's sales rep performance improvement plan (PIP) follows a structured two-stage sequence: a rep who drops below minimum KPI for two consecutive weeks enters a PIP (reverting to trainee status with intensive daily coaching); if they fail to improve over the next two weeks, they are terminated. This expectation is set at time of hire so it is not a surprise.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Sales rep on full schedule
Below minimum KPI threshold for 2 consecutive weeks

claims.text: Alex Hormozi's team meeting cadence for sales teams runs at three frequencies: daily huddles (morning training, optional for full-schedule reps but mandatory for trainees and PIPs; plus end-of-day pipeline check-in), weekly 1-on-1s for all full-schedule reps, and monthly team-wide meetings. After approximately one year of strong performance, weekly 1-on-1s may shift to bi-weekly.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Sales teams using this cadence structure
B2B or high-ticket service sales environment

claims.text: Alex Hormozi argues that sales rep conviction deteriorates over time from the monotony of a repetitive job, and this conviction loss causes sales performance to go cold. The primary mechanism for sustaining conviction is exposure to client testimonials and results, specifically assigning the testimonial readout to the rep who originally closed that client, which reinforces their personal belief in the product's impact.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Sales reps in high-volume repetitive call environments
Any product or service with documented client results
claims.mechanism: Repetitive cold calling creates emotional detachment from the product's impact. Re-exposing reps to tangible client results reconnects the transactional act of closing with the human outcome it produces. When the closing rep personally reads the testimonial of a client they sold, the connection between their behavior and the client's transformation is reinforced at the individual level.
bounded_by: Requires documented client results or testimonials to execute; teams without proof material cannot use this tactic

claims.text: Alex Hormozi argues that elite salespeople close from genuine empathy and belief in the product's transformation for the prospect, not from ego tied to being the top closer. A rep who pushes through a no because they believe in what will happen to the prospect is more effective than one who pushes through a no to win the leaderboard, because the former's conviction is authentic and perceivable by the prospect.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: High-ticket or transformational product sales
Reps dealing with resistance or objections
claims.mechanism: Prospects perceive inauthenticity in a closer who is ego-driven because the language and tone prioritize the sale over the prospect's outcome. Genuine belief in the transformation produces language that positions the rep as an advocate forcing the prospect past their own fear, which reduces resistance rather than triggering defensive reciprocity.

claims.text: Alex Hormozi structures sales team KPI competitions on a 30-to-42-day cadence (every 4-6 weeks), with competitions optimized for cash collected upfront rather than total deals or revenue. Among all competition objectives tested across Hormozi's portfolio companies, cash-up-front optimization produced the best results.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Sales teams in businesses where payment timing is variable
Service businesses where upfront vs. installment pricing is available

anchors.value: Cash collected upfront (outperformed deal count and total revenue in Hormozi portfolio)

claims.text: Alex Hormozi's speed-of-response test: during the sales hiring process, the time it takes a candidate to respond to an initial contact is treated as a proxy for work ethic. Because the company is a lead to the job-seeking candidate, fast response to the hiring company's outreach predicts the candidate's responsiveness to prospects as a rep.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Sales candidate screening
Any inbound or outbound hiring process
claims.mechanism: A job candidate is in the same psychological position as a sales lead: they want something and must decide how quickly to engage. The response latency they exhibit to the hiring company directly predicts the response latency they will show prospects, because it reflects their baseline urgency and work ethic.

examples.text: Alex Hormozi describes a period when his sales team had grown bloated. He cut more than half the team and then held a reset meeting with the survivors. He told them that being kept meant the company valued them and believed they'd buy into the vision of building a world-class sales organization. He explicitly invited anyone who didn't want the new standards to quit the next morning, no harm done, rather than drag the team through what was coming. This public standard-setting and voluntary opt-in mechanism reset the culture to one of excellence.

Hormozi uses NFL coaching as an analogy for sales management culture impact. He asks how a coach can take a losing team and bring it to near-undefeated in one season with the same players. His answer: leadership changes what the team tolerates. The same player can underperform under a permissive culture and over-perform under a high-standard culture, demonstrating that culture (the standards the manager sets and enforces) determines team output, not just individual talent.

Hormozi describes a B2B service sales call framework where all the discovery, objection pre-emption, and decision framing distill to a single binary: can we help you make more money in excess of our fee than you'd make on your own? He contrasts this with the typical broken sales call where a rep talks for 30 minutes, then presents price with no structure and no fact-finding, leaving the prospect with no clear decision to make. The contrast illustrates why script and decision clarity drive close rates.

Hormozi describes the testimonial readout practice as a three-tier conviction maintenance protocol: (1) best outcome is having a former client hop on a live sales call to share their experience, (2) second best is watching client video testimonials as a team in the morning huddle, (3) third is reading testimonials aloud, ideally having the original closer read the testimonial from the client they personally closed. The personal-closer readout is described as doubling down on the individual rep's conviction.

practices.text: During onboarding, have new sales reps listen to approximately 40 good recorded sales calls before taking any live calls. Track completion via call-review software that logs whether the rep actually watched each recording.
Role-play with trainees every morning during the 14-day onboarding period, focusing on the script. Only graduate them to a half live-call schedule after they pass the role-play test.

Listen to rep call recordings at 2x speed and take written notes before the 1-on-1 coaching session. Bold or prioritize only the top 1-2 highest-impact improvements to communicate on the call; do not overwhelm with every error.

After each 1-on-1 coaching session, send the rep a written summary of the specific items discussed so there is a trackable record. Use a tab or tracker for each rep showing the date and the items assigned each week, then verify improvement on the next weekly review.
Maintain a visual leaderboard that is always up to date and visible to the entire sales team to foster competitive motivation.
Set the PIP expectation and the bottom-10% quarterly cut rule at time of hire so reps understand the performance floor before they start; frame it as the price of being on a world-class team.

Run an optional early morning team training huddle daily. Make attendance mandatory for trainees and reps on a PIP. Observe that high-culture teams will have voluntary near-universal attendance even from tenured reps.

Boil down every offer's sales close to one binary decision (e.g., 'Can we help you make more money in excess of our fee than you'd make on your own, yes or no?') and write it into the script so reps are directing every call toward that decision.

Sales managers should exemplify every standard they require of the team: arrive first to every meeting, complete the daily checklist, follow the pipeline hygiene rules. Lead by example as the visible embodiment of team standards.

Screen for ambivert communication style in sales candidates: look for someone who listens actively, speaks when appropriate, and is socially aware. Candidates who dominate the conversation or motor-mouth are poor fits.
